Kimberly / Lina — dug into the spreadsheet and the topology diagram. Quick technical read:

- Oversubscription: 8:1 is cost-efficient but carries tail-latency risk when multiple tenants spike simultaneously. Given Acme's hard cap of 7 Gbps sustained and soft bursts to 20 Gbps, I recommend we target a conservative 4:1 oversub ratio for production pools that serve Acme's core traffic. Staging/non-critical pools can use 8:1.

- Expected latency: under 4:1, at 70% of the egress cap we project p50/p95 latency ~= 120ms / 320ms (generation path). At 8:1 under the same utilization we expect p95 to degrade toward 520-700ms during concurrent tenant surges — unacceptable for SLAs. Numbers assume packet shaping at 10ms granularity and per-connection queue depth tuning.

- Shaping granularity: EdgeCloud's typical enforcement is at the VPC egress by default, but they support per-subnet policing via TC rules if we provision the correct tagging. Recommend per-subnet policing so Acme can separate production/staging and apply different burst credit pools. We'll need EdgeCloud to enable that on their side (can you confirm, EdgeCloud?).

- Throughput target recommendation (conservative plan):
  - Sustained per-production-pool: 2,000 RPS (approx. 1.4 Gbps average, depends on prompt lengths).
  - Burst window: up to 6,000 RPS for 2 minutes with warmed caches (warm-pool standby + KV cache prefill).
  - Queueing policy: tail-drop avoidance with token-bucket smoothing, backpressure to clients at 95th percentile when queue > 150ms.

- Operational notes: pre-warm to maintain KV hit-rate >= 85% for top N prompts; we should instrument token-level cost for each pool and run a 48-hour soak test at 70% egress to validate latencies.

I'll update the workbook with a conservative sheet (nic-oversubscription-model-v1a.xlsx) reflecting these numbers; attaching recommended parameter sheet in the Drive link.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Thanks — good engineering tradeoffs laid out. A couple of operational points to surface for Acme and for our procurement annex:

- Autoscale & warm-pool cadence: If we lock 2k sustained / 6k bursts, ops needs a warm-pool of ~3% of total capacity per pool to absorb the first 30s of burst without cold-start latency. That feeds into the cost model.

- Routing fallbacks: we should include an automatic spill-to-dedicated flow when per-pool egress consumption hits 90% of the hard cap for more than a 45s window. This preserves p95 for production users at the expense of unit cost — documentable in the SLA annex.

- Billing & marketplace: Vanessa — can you confirm whether the soft-burst billing (20 Gbps short window) triggers a different marketplace SKU or a usage surcharge? Acme needs that clarified before we finalize committed capacity.

- DR & cross-region: recommend enabling cross-region spill to our eu-west or us-west warm pools as a fallback. That requires explicit consent for cross-region egress from Acme (security/compliance). Lina — will Acme allow cross-region fallback?

Action items I propose:
1) Rishi to update workbook with 4:1/8:1 variants + latency model (ETA: EOD today).
2) Vanessa to confirm billing SKU/soft-burst surcharge with Marketplace (ETA: EOD Monday).
3) Kimberly to draft a 1-page ops annex for procurement that describes shaping, spill, and testing requirements (ETA: Monday morning).
